value.value: I write fantasy novels for young adults, tackling deeper theme with approachable writing. I seek to describe the world in detail, to have the audience understand the characters through their actions and expression. A vast world awaits you, one that will evolve and develop over the course of my series.
- How much time do you typically spend writing each week?

It varies. I'd say I at least try to work a few hours a day if I can, especially since my job as a network technician can allow plenty of time. It's hard to say how much progress I've made over the past few months, as I've needed input. There's ups where I write plenty, and there's downs where I need time to recover with my favorite games, movies, shows, music and books.
- How do you integrate spiritual components so naturally without them feeling forced or preachy?

That's a balance I've strived hard to reach. I'd say the biggest thing is I want to focus on these components as being fundamental, natural truths. The gospel is a religion of truth, and if its truly the way we should live, any good, moral character should follow those truths. Thus, those who share our religion can recognize those principles at work, while those outside can hopefully appreciate them as what it means to be a good person. 

On top of that, the struggles of the characters are fundamentally spiritual struggles. Keeping them as principles everyone deals with does a good deal, and having the answers be logical and well-explained helps. But, importantly, you have to show how failing to live those principles affects someone. You must have the bad with the good. If these principles truly help one live a good life, you need to show how rejecting the principles can be worse for them.
- How do you overcome the feeling that other responsibilities are more important, which can lead to periods of inactivity?

In dealing with a complicated storyline, I appreciate the breaks that appear with responsibilities to get some distance and evaluate everything in a better light. With the nature of my job, I largely have the freedom to do what I like. I help Jeralin with chores where I can, and really, the bigger struggle is not to focus too much on my relaxing activities and actually get the hard work done. Currently, the biggest struggle is committing to the changes that the work needs to be good.
- What is your primary drive? Why do you write?

I want to make stories with purpose. I grew up with a number of good, inspirational stories that deal with human struggles in fantastical worlds. Today, there are many stories that seek simply to be a distraction, or worse, portray a lack of moral value as good. We live in a world that tears down all our inspirations to 'be realistic'. I want to form new inspirational stories to give us something to live up to again. Writing is my chosen medium to do that.
- Do you feel it helps you reach your divine purpose? How?

I do. Creating a story emulates what it is like for God to make our divine plans. I put the characters in the places they need to be to grow. They either choose the right path, or continue down the wrong, much like we do. It is up to us to be what God wants us to be, and I believe i understand better how people work as I continue to write. Through that, I understand how God works.

Take up a creative hobby, no matter what it is. Seek to inspire, but don't be outward with your intentions. Make a message that is true no matter what you believe. True things are fundamentally good things.
